[LIMP.3.3.4] **`math`, `distance` and `calendar` carry builtins.** The standard
library's modules `math`, `distance` and `calendar` each carry, besides what their source declares,
the builtin functions [LEXP.17.2] lists under their name; no other library
carries a builtin, and no author module can declare one. `math`'s source
declares three `Float` constants, each the binary64 nearest its value:

| Constant | Value | Literal |
|---|---|---|
| `pi` | π | `3.141592653589793` |
| `e` | e | `2.718281828459045` |
| `tau` | 2π | `6.283185307179586` |

`distance` and `calendar` declare nothing in source. A program reaches a member
of any of the three only through an import of it ([LIMP.3.3.2]): qualified,
`math.sin` after `import math`, or bare, `sin` after `from math import sin`
([LGRA.22.9]). A member's name is not a reserved word
([LLEX.9.6]), and the compiler must reject a use of it that no import reaches as
[LGRA.22.7] rejects an unresolved `NAME`: a call of one is
`DS_VALIDATE_UNKNOWN_FUNCTION`.
